JOURNAL_VERIFICATION_SOURCES.md calls IM-03 an Ironman scoping review, whereas the reference JSON and retrieved article describe an acute bike-fit comfort/fatigue/pain study. The scoping review in this corpus is IM-02; do not silently relabel the original journal row.

protocolCautions.detail: Abstract supports the component participant counts and 6–40 weeks / 1–4 sessions weekly. The supplied 38-study count is not independently confirmed from this abstract alone.

Different modalities and speeds have different results; no significant economy improvement for submaximal or isometric methods in this abstract. Do not extend heavy-load effects to every strength entry.
40 randomized, 22 completed; no significant between-group economy difference. Observed mechanics and measured economy remain distinct.
Recall with cueing reduced impact variables; retention was not statistically established. Do not state that six-month autonomous learning was demonstrated.

86 articles / 239 acute protocols, long intervals at least 2 min; active/passive recovery did not affect acute time near VO2max. Contrast with REC-02 mechanical outcomes, without erasing either result.
CP in this abstract also abbreviates constant-power tests, not necessarily critical power. Preserve terminology context; do not join abbreviations as identical constructs.
The authors report possible reconciliation under strict measurement criteria, not that all operational FTP, LT2, CP and MLSS estimates are interchangeable.
Six alternating 5-min trials, -15% versus level, two occasions three weeks apart; do not infer an individual D− ceiling or an unambiguous total downhill exposure absent explicit reconstruction.
11 male national-level collegiate front-crawl swimmers; CV from 200/400 m tests. Recovery periods are reported, but the abstract does not resolve every last-rest convention of a TFCL recipe.
20 km bike at 80/85/90% FTP then 5 km maximal run. Even the authors' broad 90% recommendation must not become a 180 km Ironman target.
Race correlations are not a causal training allocation. The abstract's wording about Sprint predictors is internally uneven; no dose or discipline quota follows.
20 cyclists, 45 min at 50% individual peak aerobic power in three positions. Not a 4×15 versus 6×10 aero-bout trial and not individual postural tolerance.
Metadata only: editorial with no abstract in the retrieved record; no protocol or outcome extracted.
High carbohydrate doses concern specific trained contexts, oxidation measures and a review including practitioner insight; no universal personal dose or acquired GI tolerance.

comparison.source: 20 min progressive + 3×30 s Z5 r60 s; main 5–7×3 min Z5 r3 min Z1–Z2; 10 min cool-down. The final rest policies remain unresolved in the original and candidate in V19.
comparison.studyPopulation: Narrative programming review with examples from several sports; no single intervention cohort or athlete-specific dose established.
comparison.studyProtocol: Review of work/relief intensity and duration, modality, repetitions, series and between-series recovery, plus cardiopulmonary and non-cardiopulmonary loads.
comparison.studyComparator: Programming configurations discussed in a narrative review, not a direct trial of this TFCL recipe.
comparison.studyResults: Work/recovery configuration can alter acute physiological responses; cardiorespiratory response alone does not capture all loading.
comparison.differences: No direct validation of 5–7×3 min, Z5 individual domain, 3-min recovery, final-rest occurrence, weekly frequency or VLamax-based restriction. Existing source restrictions remain unchanged.

comparison.source: 4×15 min Z2 en position aéro, r5 min Z1; unknown original final-rest occurrence; candidate totals 75 or 80 min. Source avoid: lumbar pain. The archived 6×10 alternative has another continuous exposure.
comparison.studyPopulation: 20 cyclists; results about perceptions across tested positions, not an individual Ironman cohort tolerance certificate.
comparison.studyProtocol: Three tests in randomized order, 45 min at 50% individual peak aerobic power, with different knee and trunk flexion combinations.
comparison.studyComparator: Different bicycle positions at the experimental workload, not 4×15 versus 6×10 min bouts.
comparison.studyResults: Perceptions of comfort, fatigue and pain varied across positions; upright trunk was more comfortable in the study's recreational context.
comparison.differences: Study intensity is relative to peak aerobic power, not automatically Z2/FTP. No 15-min bout tolerance, recovery duration, aerodynamic gain or equivalence of interruptions is demonstrated.
